## Natural history notes

A small owlet moth characterized by dark gray to bluish-black forewings with a distinct black wedge-shaped spot near the wing tip and subtle pale lines or shading across the wings. In Florida, it may be found in open or semi-open habitats such as fields, roadsides, forest edges, wetlands, and weedy areas where smartweeds and related low plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on smartweeds and related plants, helping move low herbaceous vegetation into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
